lpp.sweep_instruction.description: Defines the configuration rules governing cash sweep behaviour for specific accounts, including target balances and trigger thresholds. Each row represents a single sweep instruction rule, identified by a structured code indicating the group, country, account type, and index. Key identifiers include the code field (e.g. SW_GR_AE_OPERATING_1) and target_balance_ccy.
lpp.sweep_instruction.grain: One row per sweep instruction rule.

lpp.wcf_document.description: Represents individual Working Capital Finance (WCF) documents such as invoices or payment orders submitted for financing. Each record captures the document's monetary value, currency, lifecycle status (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, PAID, CANCELLED), and key dates. Key identifiers include the unique document_number (e.g. WCF-0000641) and the uuid distribution key.
lpp.wcf_document.table_type_reason: Each row is a transactional document event with an amount, status lifecycle, and date attributes — more characteristic of a fact/event table than a static dimension despite the low type confidence.
lpp.wcf_document.grain: One row per working capital finance document (invoice or payment order) identified by a unique document number.

lpp.working_capital_metric.description: Stores periodic working capital efficiency metrics computed at a reporting-period level, including Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), Days Payable Outstanding (DPO), and Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO). Each record reflects the state of working capital performance for a given period-end date in a single currency. It is used to track and benchmark cash conversion cycle components over time.
lpp.working_capital_metric.table_type_reason: Contains quantitative measures (DSO, DPO, DIO) computed per reporting period — this is a periodic snapshot fact table, not a reference table as inferred.
lpp.working_capital_metric.grain: One row per reporting period date and currency combination, capturing working capital KPI metrics.

0.description: This community represents a knowledge management area focused on capturing structured interactions with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). It contains records of individual feedback sessions, including their topics, start times, and end times. It can answer questions about the frequency, duration, and subject coverage of SME engagement activities.
query_patterns: How many SME feedback sessions were conducted on a given topic in the last quarter?
What is the average duration of SME feedback sessions by topic area?
Which topics have had the most recent SME feedback sessions recorded?

3.description: This community covers the core cash and liquidity management domain, bringing together bank account balances, cash flow transactions, sweep instructions and executions, GL balances and reconciliations, investment positions, and intercompany transactions. It provides a comprehensive view of daily cash positions across accounts, currencies, and entities, alongside the automated rules and outcomes that govern cash movement. Analysts can use this cluster to monitor liquidity health, track reconciliation variances between bank and GL records, evaluate sweep performance, and assess the combined impact of actuals versus forecasts on cash positions.
query_patterns: What is the end-of-day cash balance across all bank accounts by currency and region for a given date?
Which GL accounts have unresolved reconciliation variances above a threshold as of the latest month-end?
How much cash was swept across accounts last week, and what proportion of sweep executions failed or were skipped?

4.description: This community represents the GL account master reference data domain, providing the authoritative list of general ledger accounts used across the organization. Each account code encodes entity group, country, and purpose, serving as a key dimension for joining to balance and reconciliation data. It can answer questions about the structure and coverage of the GL chart of accounts.
query_patterns: What GL accounts are associated with a specific country or entity group?
Which GL account codes correspond to collection or operating account purposes?
How many distinct GL accounts exist per corporate entity or region?

7.description: This community serves as a reference and market data hub, combining currency master data, daily FX spot and closing rates, FX exposure forecasts, and investment instrument definitions. It underpins cross-currency analytics and hedging analysis by providing the conversion rates and instrument metadata needed to standardize exposures across the platform. It can answer questions about currency pair rates, forecasted FX exposures by tenor and direction, and the characteristics of available investment instruments.
query_patterns: What was the SPOT rate for a given currency pair on a specific date?
What is the forecasted net FX exposure (long vs. short) for a specific company and currency across tenor buckets in the next forecast period?
Which investment instruments have a credit rating above a given threshold and a maturity date within the next six months?

10.description: This community spans banking relationships, counterparty risk, FX hedging, debt and capital markets, and macroeconomic context. It brings together bank and branch reference data, credit ratings, counterparty exposure snapshots, FX forward contracts, derivative mark-to-market valuations, credit facilities, benchmark rates, letters of credit, and macroeconomic indicators. Analysts can use this cluster to monitor counterparty credit risk, evaluate the performance and fair value of hedging instruments, assess borrowing costs relative to benchmark rates, and contextualize financial positions against prevailing macro conditions.
query_patterns: What is the current mark-to-market value of all open FX forward contracts grouped by counterparty bank and currency?
How does total counterparty exposure compare against credit ratings for each banking relationship as of the latest reporting date?
What are the current all-in borrowing costs for active credit facilities relative to the latest published benchmark rates (e.g. SOFR, ESTR)?

12.description: This community covers corporate financial performance, capital allocation, forecasting, and working capital management across legal entities. It integrates company master data, financial metrics (revenue, EBITDA, FCF), capital allocation actuals versus targets, cash flow forecasts and actuals, hedge relationships, card rebate programs and earnings, equity actions, membership fee collections, and fraud loss records. This cluster supports strategic financial planning and performance management questions, including forecast accuracy, capital deployment efficiency, and the financial health of corporate entities.
query_patterns: How does actual capital allocated to CAPEX and dividends compare to the framework target percentage for each quarter by company?
What is the variance between forecasted and actual cash flows by category (e.g. PAYROLL, AP_DISBURSEMENT) for a given company and period?
Which companies have the highest fraud loss amounts by channel or fraud vector over the last rolling twelve months?

13.description: This community represents a reference catalogue of banking service types for which fees can be charged, such as wire transfers, ACH credits, and account maintenance services. It is a small lookup dimension used to classify and describe fee charge events across the platform. It can answer questions about the taxonomy of chargeable banking services and support fee analysis by service type.
query_patterns: What are all the defined banking service types and their descriptions?
Which service type codes correspond to payment-related services versus account maintenance services?
How many distinct service types are defined for use in bank fee charge classification?

14.description: This community captures the results of AI-driven query evaluation sessions, storing the original query, generated answer, evaluation timestamp, and the number of reasoning hops performed. It represents the knowledge graph intelligence layer where analytical queries are processed and assessed. It can answer questions about AI query performance, reasoning depth, and the history of questions posed to the system.
query_patterns: What queries have been evaluated by the AI brain in the last 30 days, and what answers were generated?
Which evaluated queries required the highest number of reasoning hops to produce an answer?
How has the volume of AI brain evaluation sessions trended over time?

15.description: This community represents the working capital and counterparty management domain, covering the full lifecycle of both accounts payable and accounts receivable invoices alongside working capital finance documents. It links transactional invoice data to third-party master records (retail partners, customers, and counterparties) and to application users holding finance and treasury roles. The cluster supports analysis of payment obligations, collection performance, financing activity, and operational oversight by finance teams.
query_patterns: What is the on-time payment rate for AP invoices by supplier (third party) over the last quarter?
Which AR invoices are currently overdue or written off, and which third-party customers do they belong to?
How many WCF documents are in SUBMITTED or APPROVED status, and what is their total value by currency?

17.description: This community represents the payments operations and risk domain, covering the end-to-end processing of payment transactions from file submission through individual transaction execution, ACH returns, exceptions, and fraud screening events. It combines transaction-level detail with aggregate transfer metrics and includes interest accrual records to support reconciliation of payment flows against interest-bearing positions. The cluster enables monitoring of payment success rates, failure root causes, fraud outcomes, and operational SLA performance.
query_patterns: What are the most common ACH return reason codes this month, and what is the total value of returned transactions?
How many payment exceptions were raised in the last 30 days, and what is the average resolution time in minutes by exception type?
What percentage of payment transactions in each file were rejected, and how does this correlate with fraud BLOCK decisions from the fraud detection engine?

18.description: This community represents a reference data layer for competitive benchmarking, containing a small lookup table of peer and competitor companies identified by stock ticker, sector, and peer group segment. It serves as a dimension table to contextualise comparative analysis against groups such as big-box retail, grocery, or e-commerce peers. On its own it answers basic questions about peer group composition and segmentation.
query_patterns: Which peer companies belong to the ECOMMERCE peer group segment?
How many competitor companies are tracked per sector classification?
What are the stock ticker codes for all peer companies in the GROCERY segment?

19.description: This community represents the competitive benchmarking metrics domain, storing periodic snapshots of financial and operational KPIs for peer and competitor companies. Each record captures indicators such as EBITDA, free cash flow, net debt, dividend yield, fraud losses, and payments cost ratios at a given reporting period, enabling trend and cross-company comparison. It supports strategic finance and treasury benchmarking questions about how the organisation's performance compares to industry peers.
query_patterns: How has the average EBITDA of peer companies in the retail sector trended over the last four reporting periods?
Which peer company has the lowest payments cost ratio in the most recent period?
How do fraud loss levels compare across peer companies in the ECOMMERCE segment over time?

21.description: This community represents the liquidity stress testing reference domain, providing a catalogue of named stress scenarios used to model the impact of financial shocks on liquidity positions. Each scenario is identified by a structured code and type, covering events such as AR revenue drops or adverse FX movements. This table serves as a foundational dimension for stress test execution and reporting frameworks.
query_patterns: What stress scenarios are defined for FX-related shocks, and what are their scenario type classifications?
How many distinct stress scenario types are available in the catalogue for liquidity testing?
Which stress scenarios relate to accounts receivable deterioration based on their code or description?

22.description: This community represents the cross-border payments domain, capturing individual legs of international payment transactions with details on origination and destination countries, trade corridors, FX spreads, and lifting fees. It enables granular analysis of the cost structure and volume of cross-border payment flows at the corridor level. The table supports treasury and payments teams in optimising international payment routing and understanding fee exposure.
query_patterns: What are the average FX spread and lifting fee by trade corridor over the last 90 days?
Which origination-to-destination country pairs have the highest total cross-border payment volume this quarter?
How have FX spreads on cross-border payment legs changed month over month for a specific corridor?

23.description: This community represents the card acquiring and settlement domain, covering the full lifecycle of card payment acceptance from authorization through settlement batches and chargeback disputes. It links transactional and batch-level data to acquirer reference records, contractual terms, daily SLA performance metrics, and card network definitions, enabling end-to-end oversight of card payment operations and costs. The cluster supports analysis of authorization rates, interchange and processing fees, settlement timeliness, chargeback trends, and acquirer contract compliance.
query_patterns: Which acquirer has the highest authorization approval rate this month, and how does it compare to their contracted uptime SLA?
What is the total interchange fee and net settlement amount by card network across all settlement batches in the current quarter?
How many chargebacks were initiated by reason code category in the last 60 days, and which acquirer accounts for the largest share?

glossary_terms.description: Automated Clearing House — the electronic payment network used for direct transfers. In this context refers to ACH return transactions tracked in the ach_return table.
A rejected or returned ACH payment, captured in the ach_return table with a reason code, category, date, and amount.
NACHA-standard R-codes that classify why an ACH transaction was returned (e.g. R01 = Insufficient Funds, R02 = Account Closed). Stored in ach_return.return_reason_code.
NACHA return code for Insufficient Funds — the originating account did not have enough funds to cover the transaction.
NACHA return code for Account Closed — the receiving account has been closed.
NACHA return code for No Account / Unable to Locate Account — the account number does not correspond to an open account.
NACHA return code for Unauthorized Debit — the receiver has revoked authorization for the debit entry.
NACHA return code for Unauthorized Corporate Debit — a corporate receiver has revoked authorization for a corporate debit.
NACHA return code for Customer Advises Unauthorized — the customer claims the debit was not authorized.
User-facing label for the return category INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS and return code R01. Refers to transactions returned because the sender lacked available balance.
User-facing label for the return category INVALID_ACCT. Refers to returns caused by an unrecognisable or non-existent account number.
User-facing label for the return category UNAUTHORIZED. Covers returns where the account holder disputes or revokes authorization for the transaction.
A high-level grouping of ACH return reasons stored in ach_return.return_category (INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, INVALID_ACCT, UNAUTHORIZED, OTHER). Used for bucketing and trend analysis.
The date on which an ACH return was settled or posted, stored in ach_return.return_date.
The dollar value of a returned ACH transaction, stored in ach_return.amount.
The acquiring bank or payment processor that processes card or payment transactions on behalf of a merchant. Stored in the acquirer table.
A short identifier for an acquiring institution, stored in acquirer.code. Used to link transactions and contracts to the correct processor.
Americas region — the acquirer.region database code representing North and South America.
Europe, Middle East & Africa region — the acquirer.region database code for that geographic territory.
The current state or stage of an acquirer contract, stored in acquirer_contract.contract_status (e.g. active, expired, pending).
The date on which an acquirer contract becomes valid and active, stored in acquirer_contract.effective_from.
The date on which an acquirer contract expires or is terminated, stored in acquirer_contract.effective_to.
Service Level Agreement — a contractual commitment defining minimum performance thresholds (e.g. uptime, settlement timeliness, auth rates) between an acquirer and a merchant or payment processor.
Basis Points — a unit equal to 1/100th of a percentage point (0.01%), commonly used to express processor margins, spreads, and fee rates in payment and treasury contracts.
The percentage of payment transactions successfully approved by the acquirer or card network, used as a key SLA performance metric.
The number of business days between a transaction being processed and the merchant receiving the funds; a core acquirer contract term.
The percentage of settlements completed within the contractually agreed timeframe, measuring acquirer adherence to settlement SLA commitments.
The percentage of time an acquirer's or processor's payment system is operational and available, as measured against a contractual SLA threshold.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Euro — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Euros.
ISO 4217 currency code for the US Dollar — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in US Dollars.
ISO 4217 currency code for the British Pound Sterling — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in British Pounds.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Hong Kong Dollar — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Hong Kong Dollars.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Mexican Peso — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Mexican Pesos.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Swedish Krona — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Swedish Krona.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Australian Dollar — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Australian Dollars.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Japanese Yen — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Japanese Yen.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Polish Zloty — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Polish Zloty.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Brazilian Real — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Brazilian Reals.
ISO 4217 currency code for the South Korean Won — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Korean Won.
ISO 4217 currency code for the UAE Dirham — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in UAE Dirhams.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Canadian Dollar — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Canadian Dollars.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Chinese Yuan Renminbi — used in ap_invoice.currency_code to denote invoices billed in Chinese Yuan.
Foreign Exchange currency code — the ISO 4217 three-letter code stored in ap_invoice.currency_code identifying the currency of a billed invoice.
The total monetary value of an accounts-payable invoice before any adjustments or payments applied.
The date by which an accounts-payable invoice must be paid to avoid late fees or penalties; equivalent to the payment maturity date.
The fee or spread retained by a payment processor or acquirer, expressed in basis points (bps), as defined in the acquirer contract.
The calendar date on which an acquirer SLA metric (auth rate, settlement rate, uptime) was recorded or reported.
Days Payable Outstanding — measures the average number of days a company takes to pay its supplier invoices. Derived from ap_invoice using issue_date and paid_date.
Days Sales Outstanding — measures the average number of days to collect payment after a sale. Relevant to ar_invoice aging analysis.
Month-to-Date — refers to the period from the start of the current month up to today. Maps to ap_invoice.year_month or date-range filters on issue_date or paid_date.
Year-to-Date — refers to the period from the start of the current fiscal or calendar year up to today. Applied as a date filter on issue_date, paid_date, or year_month.
Quarter-to-Date — refers to the period from the start of the current quarter up to today. Applied as a date filter on issue_date, paid_date, or year_month.
Straight-Through Processing — fully automated invoice or payment processing with no manual intervention. Relevant to invoice status flows (OPEN → PAID without DISPUTED or PARTIAL stops).
Working Capital — the difference between current assets and current liabilities. In this context, influenced by outstanding AP (ap_invoice) and AR (ar_invoice) balances.
The ratio of invoices paid on or before their due date, per payment terms. Maps directly to ap_invoice.on_time_rate.
Coded conditions defining when payment is due (e.g. NET_30 = net 30 days, EOM_5 = end of month plus 5 days). Maps to ap_invoice.payment_terms.
The current state of an AP invoice. Database codes are PAID, OPEN, PARTIAL, DISPUTED. Users may say 'paid', 'open', 'partially paid', or 'disputed'.
The supplier or payee that issues an AP invoice. Users say 'vendor' but the database may refer to the party as supplier or payee.
Unique identifier for an AP invoice. Maps to ap_invoice.invoice_number.
The date an AP invoice was issued. Maps to ap_invoice.issue_date.
The date an AP invoice was paid or settled. Maps to ap_invoice.paid_date.
The month or fiscal period an AP invoice belongs to. Maps to ap_invoice.year_month.
The gross invoiced amount before any payments. Maps to ap_invoice.total_billed.
The total amount remitted against an invoice. Maps to ap_invoice.total_paid.
The currency in which an AR invoice is billed or settled. Maps to ar_invoice.currency_code. Users may say 'Euro', 'US Dollar', 'Sterling', 'Won', etc.
Unit multiplier equal to 1,000,000. Users may express invoice amounts as '2M' or '2 million'; should be converted to numeric values when filtering total_billed or total_paid.
Unit multiplier equal to 1,000,000,000. Users may express amounts as '1B' or '1 billion'; should be converted to numeric values when filtering amounts.
Unit equal to 0.01% (one hundredth of a percentage point). Used when discussing rate changes or on_time_rate variances in treasury and finance contexts.
Ratio expressed as a value out of 100. Used with on_time_rate and similar ratio columns; users may say '95%' meaning 0.95 in the database.
The unpaid portion of an invoice, calculated as total_billed minus total_paid. Relevant for OPEN and PARTIAL status invoices.
An invoice that has not been paid by its due date as determined by payment_terms applied to issue_date. Inversely related to on_time_rate.
Accounts Receivable — in this context ARR may refer to the AR (Accounts Receivable) ledger or portfolio of outstanding invoices tracked in ar_invoice.
Mark-to-Market — the practice of valuing open receivables or foreign-currency balances at current market rates. Relevant to multi-currency bank_statement_balance records.
Foreign Exchange — refers to currency conversion considerations across the multi-currency balances in bank_statement_balance.currency_code (USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, JPY, MXN, etc.).
Payment terms requiring the invoice to be paid within 30 days of the invoice date. Maps to database code NET_30 in ar_invoice.payment_terms.
Payment terms requiring the invoice to be paid within 60 days of the invoice date. Maps to database code NET_60 in ar_invoice.payment_terms.
Payment terms requiring the invoice to be paid within 90 days of the invoice date. Maps to database code NET_90 in ar_invoice.payment_terms.
Payment terms requiring immediate payment upon receipt of the invoice. Maps to database code NET_0 in ar_invoice.payment_terms.
Invoice status indicating the invoice has been fully settled. Maps to database value PAID in ar_invoice.status.
Invoice status indicating the invoice is outstanding and awaiting payment. Maps to database value OPEN in ar_invoice.status.
Invoice status indicating the receivable has been deemed uncollectable and removed from active AR. Maps to database value WRITTEN_OFF in ar_invoice.status.
Data quality validation status indicating a bank statement balance record has passed all quality checks. Maps to PASSED in bank_statement_balance.quality_status.
Data quality validation status indicating a bank statement balance record has failed one or more quality checks. Maps to FAILED in bank_statement_balance.quality_status.
A billing document issued to a customer representing an amount owed. Stored in the ar_invoice table. Users may refer to it by several aliases.
The date the invoice was created or raised, stored in ar_invoice.issue_date. Used for aging and DSO calculations.
The date on which an invoice was settled or payment was received, stored in ar_invoice.paid_date. Used for DSO and collection performance analysis.
The closing balance on a bank account as recorded in bank_statement_balance.amount. Used for liquidity and cash position reporting.
An invoice where the current date exceeds ar_invoice.due_date and status is still OPEN. A key treasury collection metric.
The bucketing of open receivables by how long they have been outstanding (e.g. 0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ days). Derived from ar_invoice.due_date or issue_date vs. current date.
Bank Identifier Code — a standardised code used to identify banks internationally for wire and SWIFT transactions. Maps to the bank.bic column.
Legal Entity Identifier — a globally unique regulatory code assigned to legal entities participating in financial transactions. Maps to the bank.lei column.
A financial institution holding accounts. Users may refer to banks as lenders or counterparties; the database represents these in the bank table via bank.description1.
A specific account held at a bank. Users may refer to it by various identifiers or codes. Maps to the bank_account table.
An internal identifier for a bank within the treasury system. Maps to bank.code. Users may call it a bank key, bank slug, or internal bank ID.
The date as of which a bank statement balance is reported. Maps to bank_statement_balance.statement_date.
The date on which account-level data (balances, counts) was aggregated or rolled up. Maps to bank_account.rollup_date.
The total cash held across one or more bank accounts at a point in time. Maps to bank_account.total_cash.
The number of bank accounts associated with an entity or rollup. Maps to bank_account.n_accounts.
A standardised code (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP) denoting the denomination of a bank account. Maps to bank_account.currency.
Abbreviation for Asia-Pacific, used as the database value for the bank_branch.region dimension when users refer to the Asia-Pacific geographic region.
Abbreviation for Latin America, used as the database value for the bank_branch.region dimension when users refer to the Latin America geographic region.
Abbreviation for Middle East & North Africa, used as the database value for the bank_branch.region dimension when users refer to that sub-region.
Standardised two- or three-letter code representing a country, stored in bank_branch.country_code. Users may refer to this simply as 'country' or 'nation code'.
The maximum monetary amount a signatory is authorised to approve or execute on a bank account, stored in bank_account_signatory.authority_limit_amount.
The date by which a bank account signatory's authorisation must be reviewed and renewed, stored in bank_account_signatory.next_recertify_due_date.

The role or authority level assigned to a bank account signatory (e.g. sole signatory, co-signatory), stored in bank_account_signatory.role. Users may call this 'signatory type', 'account role', or 'mandate role'.

The current active/inactive or authorisation state of a bank account signatory, stored in bank_account_signatory.status. Users may call this 'mandate status', 'active flag', or 'account access status'.
The unique identifier for a bank branch, stored in bank_branch.code. Users may refer to this as 'branch ID', 'branch key', 'branch reference', or 'location code'.
The date on which a bank fee was charged or billed, stored in bank_fee.charge_date. Users may call this 'billing date', 'transaction date', 'charge day', or 'debit date'.
The monetary value of a bank fee that was charged, stored in bank_fee.charged_amount. Users may refer to this as 'charge amount', 'billed amount', 'fee total', or 'debit amount'.
The currency in which a bank fee is denominated, stored in bank_fee.currency_code. Users may call this 'currency', 'currency type', 'billing currency', or 'denomination'.
A wire transfer payment method. Users may reference 'wire' or 'wires' when filtering bank fees by transaction or payment type associated with wire instructions.

A bank mandate defines the authorised signatories and their signing rules for a bank account. Users may say 'mandate' when referring to records in bank_account_signatory, including role, status, and authority limit.

An individual authorised to operate a bank account on behalf of an entity, represented as a record in bank_account_signatory. Users may also call this an 'authorised user', 'account signer', or 'mandate holder'.
A physical or logical branch of a bank, represented in the bank_branch table. Users may refer to this as 'branch', 'bank location', or 'branch office'.
A charge levied by a bank for services rendered, represented in the bank_fee table. Users may call this a 'bank charge', 'service fee', 'account fee', or 'banking cost'.
Indicates a bank fee record has been marked for review or raised an exception. Maps to boolean TRUE in the database column bank_fee.flagged.
Indicates a bank fee record has not been marked for review. Maps to boolean FALSE in the database column bank_fee.flagged.
A short identifier for a bank service type, stored in bank_service_type.code. Users may refer to it as a fee code or transaction type code.
The human-readable label for a bank service type, stored in bank_service_type.description. Users often say 'service name' or 'fee description' instead of 'description'.
A dimension on tribal_knowledge_fact indicating how reliable or trustworthy a recorded fact is. Users may express this as certainty, trust level, or accuracy rating.
The timestamp when a tribal knowledge fact was recorded or logged, stored in tribal_knowledge_fact.captured_at.
A classification dimension on tribal_knowledge_fact that categorises the nature of a recorded insight or piece of knowledge.
The lifecycle state of a tribal knowledge fact record, stored in tribal_knowledge_fact.status. Users may refer to it as record status, active status, or current status.
Free-text field on tribal_knowledge_fact holding explanatory notes or commentary about a recorded fact. Users often say 'description', 'notes', or 'details'.
Real-Time Payments — an instant payment rail. May appear as a service code or service type label in bank_service_type when categorising real-time payment fees.
The Federal Reserve's instant payment service. May appear as a bank service type code or description when classifying instant-payment bank fees.
Days Inventory Outstanding — the average number of days inventory is held before sale. May be referenced in tribal_knowledge_fact narratives related to working capital.
Other Comprehensive Income — gains and losses excluded from net income. May appear in tribal_knowledge_fact narratives or fact_type classifications for hedging or investment entries.
Weighted Average Cost of Capital — the blended rate a company pays across all its capital sources. May be captured as a tribal knowledge fact or referenced in narratives.

variants: Earnings Before Interest Taxes Depreciation and Amortization
glossary_terms.description: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation — a proxy for operating cash flow. May be referenced in tribal_knowledge_fact narratives or as a fact_type.
A weighted average interest or fee rate across multiple instruments or service types. Users may reference this when analysing bank fee rates across service codes.
The proportion of an exposure that is hedged. May be stored or referenced in tribal_knowledge_fact records with fact_type related to hedging strategy.

Loan-to-Value or Lifetime Value — either the ratio of a loan to the value of an asset, or the total revenue expected from a customer. Context determines which meaning applies in tribal knowledge facts.
Euro Short-Term Rate — the overnight benchmark interest rate for the Euro, published by the ECB. Maps to benchmark_code = 'ESTR' and currency_code = 'EUR'.
Secured Overnight Financing Rate — the USD overnight benchmark rate replacing LIBOR, based on US Treasury repo transactions. Maps to benchmark_code = 'SOFR' and currency_code = 'USD'.
Sterling Overnight Index Average — the GBP overnight benchmark rate published by the Bank of England. Maps to benchmark_code = 'SONIA' and currency_code = 'GBP'.
Tokyo Overnight Average Rate — the JPY overnight benchmark rate published by the Bank of Japan. Maps to benchmark_code = 'TONA' and currency_code = 'JPY'.
Mexican Interbank Rate (28-day tenor) — the MXN floating reference rate used in Mexican money markets. Maps to benchmark_code = 'TIIE_28D' and currency_code = 'MXN'.
Swiss Average Rate Overnight — the CHF overnight benchmark rate replacing LIBOR CHF. Maps to benchmark_code = 'SARON' and currency_code = 'CHF'.

Euro Interbank Offered Rate (3-month tenor) — the 3-month EUR term benchmark rate widely used for floating-rate instruments. Maps to benchmark_code = 'EURIBOR_3M', tenor = '3M', currency_code = 'EUR'.
Australian Bank Bill Swap Rate (3-month tenor) — the AUD 3-month term benchmark rate. Maps to benchmark_code = 'AUD_BBSW_3M', tenor = '3M', currency_code = 'AUD'.
US Treasury Bill (3-month tenor) — the 3-month US T-Bill rate used as a risk-free benchmark. Maps to benchmark_code = 'T_BILL_3M', tenor = '3M', currency_code = 'USD'.
HKD Overnight Index Average — the Hong Kong Dollar overnight benchmark rate. Maps to benchmark_code = 'HONIA' and currency_code = 'HKD'.
Certificado de Depósito Interbancário — the Brazilian overnight interbank benchmark rate. Maps to benchmark_code = 'CDI' and currency_code = 'BRL'.
Singapore Overnight Rate Average — the SGD overnight benchmark rate published by the MAS. Maps to benchmark_code = 'SORA' and currency_code = 'SGD'.
Canadian Dollar Offered Rate — the CAD short-term benchmark rate. Maps to benchmark_code = 'CDOR' and currency_code = 'CAD'.
Overnight tenor — the shortest standard rate term, representing a one-business-day period. Maps to tenor = 'ON' in the benchmark_rate table.
1-Month tenor — a one-calendar-month rate period. Maps to tenor = '1M' in the benchmark_rate table.
3-Month tenor — a three-calendar-month rate period. Maps to tenor = '3M' in the benchmark_rate table.
Swiss Franc — the currency of Switzerland. Maps to currency_code = 'CHF'.
Singapore Dollar — the currency of Singapore. Maps to currency_code = 'SGD'.
The published reference interest rate for a given currency and tenor on a specific date. Stored in benchmark_rate.rate and identified by benchmark_code, currency_code, tenor, and rate_date.
The date on which a benchmark rate is officially published or observed. Maps to benchmark_rate.rate_date.
A committed borrowing arrangement between a borrower and lender. Represented in the credit_facility table, identified by credit_facility.code.
The total maximum amount a lender has committed to make available under a credit facility. Maps to credit_facility.commitment_amount.
The unique identifier for a credit facility in the database. Maps to credit_facility.code.
The benchmark rate tied to a credit facility's interest calculation. Maps to credit_facility.benchmark_code.
The logical rule or event that activates a piece of tribal knowledge or a system action. Maps to tribal_knowledge_fact.trigger_condition.
The short descriptive heading identifying a tribal knowledge entry. Maps to tribal_knowledge_fact.title.
Abbreviation for currency, used to identify the denomination of a borrowing. Maps to currency_code in the borrowing table.
The total effective interest rate on a borrowing, inclusive of the benchmark rate and credit spread. Maps to borrowing.all_in_rate. Also referred to as cost of funds or effective rate.
The margin charged above a benchmark rate on a credit facility, expressed in basis points. Maps to credit_facility.spread_bps.
The face value or notional amount of a borrowing, typically expressed in the loan currency. Maps to borrowing.principal_amount.
Database status code indicating a borrowing that has not yet been repaid and remains active. Maps to borrowing.status = 'OUTSTANDING'. Users may refer to this as 'active', 'open', or 'live' loans.
Database status code indicating a borrowing that has been fully repaid. Maps to borrowing.status = 'REPAID'. Users may refer to this as 'closed', 'settled', or 'paid off'.
The date on which a financial obligation is due for repayment or a facility expires. Maps to both borrowing.repayment_date (loan level) and credit_facility.maturity_date (facility level).
The date on which funds are disbursed under a borrowing. Maps to borrowing.drawdown_date.
The date on which a credit facility becomes active or legally effective. Maps to credit_facility.start_date.
The lifecycle state of a credit facility or borrowing. Maps to credit_facility.status and borrowing.status. Users may describe this as deal status, credit line status, or loan state.
An individual loan drawdown or utilisation under a credit facility. Referred to in the database as the borrowing table. Users may call this a loan, draw, tranche, or utilisation.
Capital Expenditures — funds deployed for long-term asset investment. Maps to the CAPEX bucket code in capital_allocation_actual.
Mergers & Acquisitions — capital allocated toward acquiring or merging with other entities. Maps to the M_AND_A bucket code in capital_allocation_actual.
Dividend payments — capital returned to shareholders as distributions. Maps to the DIVIDENDS bucket code in capital_allocation_actual.
Debt Paydown — capital used to repay or reduce outstanding debt obligations. Maps to the DEBT_PAYDOWN bucket code in capital_allocation_actual.
Share Buybacks — capital allocated to repurchase the company's own shares from the market. Maps to the BUYBACKS bucket code in capital_allocation_actual.
User-facing term for the 'bucket' column in capital_allocation_actual, which categorizes how capital is deployed (e.g. CAPEX, M&A, Dividends).
User-facing term for the actual monetary amount disbursed in a capital allocation, corresponding to the 'amount' column in capital_allocation_actual.
The planned or framework-defined percentage share for a capital allocation category, corresponding to framework_target_pct in capital_allocation_actual.
The as-of or period-end date for a capital allocation record, corresponding to period_date in capital_allocation_actual.
The monetary value of a card authorization event, corresponding to the 'amount' column in card_authorization.
3D Secure — a card authentication protocol used to verify cardholder identity during online transactions. Outcome stored in card_authorization.auth_3ds_status.
User-facing label for the free-text summary of a brain evaluation result, corresponding to the answer_summary column in brain_evaluation.
The input question or prompt submitted for evaluation, corresponding to the query_text column in brain_evaluation.
The timestamp or date when a brain evaluation was processed or assessed, corresponding to evaluated_at in brain_evaluation.
A measure of reasoning or traversal depth in the brain evaluation process — how many hops or steps were taken to expand a query. Corresponds to expansion_hops in brain_evaluation.
Card Not Present — indicates a transaction where the physical card was not used at a terminal (e.g. online or phone purchases). Maps to cnp_indicator = true in the database.
The process by which a card transaction is approved or declined by the issuer. Represented in the card_authorization table.
User-facing label for a successful authorization outcome. Maps to decision = 'APPROVED' in the database.
User-facing label for a rejected authorization. Maps to decision = 'DECLINED' in the database.
User-facing label for an authorization that did not receive a response in time. Maps to decision = 'TIMEOUT' in the database.
User-facing label for an authorization that resulted in a system or processing error. Maps to decision = 'ERROR' in the database.
Indicates a face-to-face transaction where the physical card was present at the terminal. Maps to cnp_indicator = false in the database.
The coded reason why an authorization was declined. Stored in decline_reason_code. Users may refer to this as rejection reason, refusal code, or denial reason.
The time taken in milliseconds from sending an authorization request to receiving a response. Stored in response_time_ms. Key metric for SLA monitoring.
The timestamp when an authorization request was sent. Stored in auth_request_ts. Used as the start boundary for latency and time-series analysis.
The timestamp when an authorization response was received. Stored in auth_response_ts. Used as the end boundary for latency calculations.
The total value of settled sales transactions within a batch, before any deductions. Stored in card_settlement_batch.gross_sales.
The number of individual transactions included in a settlement batch. Stored in card_settlement_batch.batch_count.
A categorical grouping of transactions by their monetary value range (e.g. low, medium, high spend). Stored in transaction_size_band. Used for segmentation and analysis.
The percentage of authorization requests that result in an APPROVED decision. A key treasury and payments performance metric derived from the decision field.
The percentage of authorization requests that result in a DECLINED decision. Derived from the decision field. Inverse of approval rate.
A grouped set of card transactions submitted together for clearing and settlement. Represented in the card_settlement_batch table.

Fee paid to the card-issuing bank as a percentage of each transaction, deducted from gross sales to arrive at net settlement. Stored in card_settlement_batch.interchange and card_settlement_batch.interchange_amount.

The final amount deposited to the merchant after deducting interchange, network assessments, and processor fees from gross sales. Stored in card_settlement_batch.net_settlement and card_settlement_batch.net_settlement_amount.
Fee charged by the card network brand (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) on transaction volume, separate from interchange. Stored in card_settlement_batch.network_assess.
The total face value of card transactions before any fees or deductions are applied. Stored in card_settlement_batch.gross_sales_amount.
The calendar date on which transaction data is aggregated into a settlement batch for reporting. Stored in card_settlement_batch.rollup_date.
The exact date and time when settled funds are credited to the merchant's bank account. Stored in card_settlement_batch.bank_deposit_ts.
The date and time at which a card settlement batch is finalized and closed for processing. Stored in card_settlement_batch.batch_close_ts.
User-facing term for the date a batch is summarized and settled; maps to card_settlement_batch.rollup_date in the database.
User-facing term for the net amount paid out to the merchant; maps to card_settlement_batch.net_settlement / net_settlement_amount in the database.
The card scheme or brand (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) that facilitates card transaction routing and charges assessment fees. Referenced via network_assess synonyms such as 'brand fee' and 'scheme fee'.
Regional/informal alias for interchange fee, commonly used in certain markets. Maps to card_settlement_batch.interchange and card_settlement_batch.interchange_amount.
European/regional alias for the network assessment fee charged by a card scheme. Maps to card_settlement_batch.network_assess.
The effective percentage of gross sales retained after all fees (interchange, network assessment, processor margin), derived by dividing net_settlement_amount by gross_sales_amount.

Blended percentage cost of card acceptance calculated as total fees (interchange + network assessment + processor margin) divided by gross sales amount; a key treasury metric for monitoring card processing costs.
User-facing term for the aggregate gross transaction dollar value processed in a batch or period. Maps to card_settlement_batch.gross_sales_amount.
The elapsed time between batch_close_ts and bank_deposit_ts, representing how long it takes for settled card funds to reach the merchant's bank account. A key treasury liquidity metric.
Visa card network. Maps to the database code 'VISA' in card_network.code.
Mastercard card network. Maps to the database code 'MASTERCARD' in card_network.code.
American Express card network. Maps to the database code 'AMEX' in card_network.code.
Discover card network. Maps to the database code 'DISCOVER' in card_network.code.
Costco-branded private label card network. Maps to the database code 'COSTCO_PRIVATE' in card_network.code.
UnionPay card network, a major Chinese payment scheme. Maps to the database code 'UNIONPAY' in card_network.code.
A card network type representing store-branded or issuer-specific cards not on open networks. Maps to the database value 'PRIVATE_LABEL' in card_network.network_type.
Credit card network type — cards where the balance is paid later. Maps to the database value 'CREDIT' in card_network.network_type.
Charge card network type — cards where the full balance must be paid each cycle (e.g. traditional Amex). Maps to the database value 'CHARGE' in card_network.network_type.
PIN-authenticated debit card network type — transactions verified via personal identification number. Maps to the database value 'DEBIT_PIN' in card_network.network_type.
The fee charged by a card network (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) to the acquirer/processor per settlement batch. Stored in card_settlement_batch.network_assessment_amount.
The date and time at which the processor/acquirer finalised and settled a card batch. Stored in card_settlement_batch.processor_settle_ts.
The portion of card spend that qualifies for rebate calculation under the rebate programme terms. Stored in card_rebate_earning.eligible_spend.
The rebate amount earned by the organisation from the card network or issuer for a given period, based on eligible spend. Stored in card_rebate_earning.rebate_earned.
The reporting or statement date associated with a rebate earning record, used to identify which period the rebate applies to. Stored in card_rebate_earning.period_date.
A user-facing synonym for a card network (e.g. Visa, Mastercard). Maps to card_network.name in the database.
The short identifier used in the database to represent a card network (e.g. VISA, AMEX). Stored in card_network.code.
A classification of the card network by payment method category (e.g. Credit, Debit PIN, Private Label, Charge). Stored in card_network.network_type.
The classification of a card transaction by the type of purchase or merchant, stored in card_rebate_earning.spend_category.
The unique identifier for a card rebate program, stored in card_rebate_program.code.
The classification or category of a card rebate program, stored in card_rebate_program.program_type.
The rebate rate in basis points earned when program spend targets are met, stored in card_rebate_program.rebate_bps_at_target.
A flag indicating whether a card settlement transaction was made across international borders (true) as opposed to domestic (false), stored in card_settlement_line.cross_border.
The total pre-net settlement value of a card transaction before any fees or adjustments, stored in card_settlement_line.gross_amount.
The card network interchange fee expressed in basis points, representing the rate charged per transaction, stored in card_settlement_line.interchange_bps.
The country code of the bank that issued the card used in the settlement transaction, stored in card_settlement_line.issuer_country.
The date as of which a cash balance is reported or valued, stored in cash_balance.balance_date.
A financial incentive paid back to the cardholder organization based on card spend volume and program terms, calculated using rebate basis points against eligible spend.
Indicates a card settlement transaction where the issuer country matches the transaction country (cross_border = false). Opposite of Cross-Border.
The finalized clearing and payment of a card transaction between the merchant, card network, and issuing bank, represented in the card_settlement_line table.
The net available cash balance across accounts at a point in time, derived from cash_balance.amount. Used in daily liquidity and treasury reporting.
A leverage ratio stored in company_financial_metric.debt_to_ebitda that measures how many years of EBITDA would be needed to repay total debt. Also referred to as net leverage or credit ratio.
Earnings Per Share. Specifically refers to diluted EPS in the database (company_financial_metric.diluted_eps), representing net income divided by diluted share count.
The legal or organizational entity stored in the company table. Users may refer to this as a firm, organization, or entity, all mapping to the same company records.
A short code identifying a company, stored in company.code. Users may call this an entity code, firm code, or organization code.
A disputed or reversed payment transaction tracked in the chargeback table. Users may also refer to these as disputes, reversals, or claims.
The current state of a chargeback case, stored in chargeback.status. Users may call this dispute status, case status, resolution status, or chargeback state.
A card-network-issued code categorizing the reason for a chargeback, stored in chargeback.reason_code. Users may call this a dispute code, reversal code, or claim code.
A higher-level grouping of chargeback reason codes stored in chargeback.reason_category. Users may call this the dispute reason group, reason group, or claim reason.
The date a chargeback case was closed or settled, stored in chargeback.resolved_date. Users may refer to this as the close date, settlement date, case closed date, or decision date.
The geographic domicile of a company, stored in company.country. Users may refer to this as nation, geography, location, or domicile.
The registered or official name of a company, stored in company.name. Users may refer to this as the firm name, entity name, organization name, or company name.
Free Cash Flow. Mapped to company_financial_metric.free_cash_flow. Represents cash generated after capital expenditures; a key liquidity metric in treasury.
Trailing Twelve Months. A value of the period_type code in company_financial_metric.period_type. Refers to the most recent 12-month rolling financial period.
Full Year. A value of the period_type code in company_financial_metric.period_type. Refers to an annual fiscal reporting period.
Quarterly. A value of the period_type code in company_financial_metric.period_type. Refers to a three-month fiscal reporting period.
Total financial debt minus cash and cash equivalents. Mapped to company_financial_metric.net_debt. Used in treasury to assess a company's true leverage position.
Total top-line income from operations. Mapped to company_financial_metric.revenue. Represents gross or net sales reported for the period.
Total share count including all dilutive securities such as options and convertibles. Mapped to company_financial_metric.diluted_shares_outstanding. Used in per-share financial calculations.
The end date of a financial reporting period. Mapped to company_financial_metric.period_date. Used to filter or anchor financial metrics to a specific point in time.
Classification of the financial reporting window (e.g. Quarterly, Full Year, TTM). Mapped to company_financial_metric.period_type. Accepts coded values: Q, FY, TTM.
The reference date for a counterparty exposure snapshot. Mapped to counterparty_exposure.as_of_date. Indicates the point-in-time at which exposure values are calculated.
The currency code in which counterparty exposure values are denominated. Mapped to counterparty_exposure.reporting_currency. Stored as ISO currency codes (e.g. USD, EUR).
A monetary value associated with financial metrics such as revenue, EBITDA, FCF, and net debt. Users may express these in full units, thousands (K), millions (M/mm), or billions (B/bn).

An external party to a financial transaction or exposure, such as a bank, broker, or trading partner. Referenced in counterparty_exposure table. Users may refer to this as a bank, lender, or trading partner.
The markup or difference between the mid-market exchange rate and the rate applied to a cross-border payment, expressed in basis points (BPS). Maps to cross_border_payment_leg.fx_spread_bps.
Fees charged to process or transfer a cross-border payment, sometimes called wire fees or transaction charges. Maps to cross_border_payment_leg.lifting_fees.
The aggregate financial exposure to a counterparty, representing the total outstanding risk amount. Maps to counterparty_exposure.total_exposure.
A standardised score or grade assigned by a rating agency to indicate the creditworthiness of an entity. Maps to credit_rating.rating_grade.
The organisation that issues a credit rating (e.g. Moody's, S&P, Fitch). Users may refer to these by common names that differ from database codes. Maps to credit_rating.agency.
Database code for Moody's Investors Service, a major credit rating agency. Users typically say 'Moody's'; the database stores 'MOODYS'.
Database code for S&P Global Ratings (Standard & Poor's). Users say 'S&P' or 'Standard & Poor's'; the database stores 'SP'.
Database code for Fitch Ratings. Users say 'Fitch'; the database stores 'FITCH'.
The forward-looking direction or trend of a credit rating (e.g. Stable, Positive, Negative, Watch). Maps to credit_rating.outlook.
Database code for a 'Stable' rating outlook, indicating no expected near-term rating change. Users say 'Stable'; the database stores 'STABLE'.
Database code for a 'Positive' rating outlook, indicating a potential upgrade. Users say 'Positive'; the database stores 'POSITIVE'.
Database code for a 'Negative' rating outlook, indicating a potential downgrade. Users say 'Negative'; the database stores 'NEGATIVE'.
Database code for a 'Watch' rating outlook, indicating the rating is under active review for a possible change. Users say 'Watch' or 'on watch'; the database stores 'WATCH'.
A flag indicating whether a credit rating record is the latest active rating (true) versus a historical one (false). Maps to credit_rating.is_current.
A defined cross-border route between two regions or countries along which payments flow (e.g. US to Europe, Europe to Asia-Pacific). Maps to cross_border_payment_leg.corridor.
Database code for the US to Europe payment corridor. Users may say 'US to Europe' or 'United States to Europe'; the database stores 'US-EU'.
Database code for the Europe to Asia-Pacific payment corridor. Users may say 'Europe to Asia-Pacific' or 'Europe to APAC'; the database stores 'EU-APAC'.
Database code for the US to Asia-Pacific payment corridor. Users may say 'US to Asia-Pacific' or 'US to APAC'; the database stores 'US-APAC'.
Database code for the US to Mexico payment corridor. Users may say 'US to Mexico' or 'United States to Mexico'; the database stores 'US-MX'.
Database code for the US to Canada payment corridor. Users may say 'US to Canada' or 'United States to Canada'; the database stores 'US-CA'.

The receiving country in a cross-border payment, identified by ISO country code (e.g. MX, GB, JP). Users may refer to it as the beneficiary country, payee country, or target country. Maps to cross_border_payment_leg.destination_country.
The date on which a derivative position is priced or marked to market. Maps to derivative_mtm.valuation_date.
The monetary fair value of a derivative instrument at a given valuation date, which can reflect an unrealized gain or loss. Maps to derivative_mtm.mtm_amount.
The currency in which a derivative's mark-to-market value is denominated or reported. Maps to derivative_mtm.mtm_currency.
The ISO country code representing the country from which a cross-border payment leg originates. Maps to cross_border_payment_leg.origination_country.
The full descriptive name of a currency (e.g. 'US Dollar', 'Euro'). Maps to currency.description.
An external counterparty, customer, or partner referenced in treasury transactions. Maps to the third_party table.
A unique identifier for an external counterparty or partner. Maps to third_party.code.
The display name of an external counterparty or partner. Maps to third_party.name.
The date on which an equity corporate action (e.g. dividend, buyback) takes effect or is recorded. Maps to equity_action.action_date.
The category or classification of an equity corporate action event. Maps to equity_action.action_type. Known aliases: Buyback → BUYBACK, Dividend → DIVIDEND, Special Dividend → SPECIAL_DIVIDEND.
A corporate action representing a standard cash or stock distribution to shareholders. Stored as code 'DIVIDEND' in equity_action.action_type.
A one-time or non-recurring corporate action distribution to shareholders, distinct from a regular dividend. Stored as code 'SPECIAL_DIVIDEND' in equity_action.action_type.
A corporate action where a company repurchases its own shares from the market. Stored as code 'BUYBACK' in equity_action.action_type.
A payment transaction that crosses national boundaries, tracked at the leg level including origination country. Maps to the cross_border_payment_leg table.
The paper profit or loss on an open derivative position based on current market value versus book value, before settlement. Maps to derivative_mtm.mtm_amount.
Dividend Per Share — the dollar amount of dividend paid out for each share of stock, stored in equity_action.dividend_per_share.
The price paid or received per individual share in an equity action (e.g. buyback or issuance), stored in equity_action.price_per_share.
The number of shares involved in an equity action, stored in equity_action.shares.
The total monetary value of an equity action (shares × price, or total dividend payout), stored in equity_action.total_amount.
The contractually agreed fee rate on a rate card, stored in fee_rate_card.negotiated_rate.
The ISO currency code used to denominate a transaction or fee, stored as currency_code in fee_rate_card and forecast_cash_flow.
Tax Payment — scheduled cash outflows for tax obligations. Stored as the value TAX in forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.
Accounts Receivable Collection — expected cash inflows from collecting outstanding receivables. Stored as AR_COLLECTION in forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.
Intercompany Transfer — cash flows between legal entities within the same corporate group. Stored as INTERCOMPANY in forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.
Debt Service — cash outflows covering principal repayments and interest payments on debt obligations. Stored as DEBT_SERVICE in forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.
Accounts Payable Disbursement — cash outflows to vendors or suppliers for goods and services. Stored as AP_DISBURSEMENT in forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.
Payroll — cash outflows for employee compensation and wages. Stored as the value PAYROLL in forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.
The date or period for which a cash flow is projected, stored in forecast_cash_flow.forecast_date.
The projected monetary value of a forecasted cash flow, stored in forecast_cash_flow.forecast_amount.
The category or classification of a cash flow (e.g. CAPEX, TAX, PAYROLL), stored as a code in forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.
Basis Points — a unit equal to 1/100th of a percentage point (0.01%), commonly used to express fee rates and negotiated rates in treasury contexts such as fee_rate_card.negotiated_rate.
A unit multiplier representing 1,000,000, commonly used by users when expressing large monetary amounts such as forecast_amount or total_amount (e.g. '$5 million').
A unit multiplier representing 1,000,000,000, commonly used by users when expressing very large monetary amounts in treasury forecasting contexts (e.g. '$2 billion').
A unit expressing a rate or ratio as parts per hundred, used when referencing negotiated fee rates or dividend rates (e.g. '2.5%').

A short-term cash flow forecasting snapshot produced monthly, projecting cash flows over a 13-week (rolling quarter) horizon using the direct method (i.e., based on actual cash receipts and disbursements).
A medium-to-long-term cash flow forecasting snapshot produced quarterly, projecting cash flows over an 18-month horizon using the indirect method (i.e., derived from P&L and balance sheet movements).
FX Revaluation — database code for non-cash or cash impacts arising from the revaluation of foreign currency-denominated balances at period-end exchange rates.

The difference between the forecasted (planned) amount and the actual (realized) amount for a given cash flow category and period. Can be expressed as an absolute amount (variance_amount) or a percentage (variance_pct).
The variance between forecast and actual amounts expressed as a percentage of the forecast amount, used to measure forecast accuracy. Also referred to as 'percent deviation' or 'budget variance %'.
The realized or booked cash flow amounts recorded after the fact, as opposed to forecasted/planned amounts. Stored in the actual_amount column.
The planned or projected cash flow amount captured in a forecast snapshot, against which actuals are later compared to derive variance.
The unique identifier assigned to a forecast snapshot run, used to reference or join a specific forecast instance in the database.

A cash flow forecasting methodology that projects cash receipts and disbursements directly from operational data (e.g., AR, AP, payroll schedules), as referenced in the 'Monthly 13-week direct forecast' snapshot type.

A cash flow forecasting methodology that derives cash flows from net income adjusted for non-cash items and working capital changes, as referenced in the 'Quarterly 18-month indirect forecast' snapshot type.
A measure of how closely forecasted cash flow amounts match actual realized amounts, typically expressed via variance_pct. A lower absolute variance % indicates higher forecast accuracy.
Fraud detection decision code indicating a transaction was permitted to proceed without intervention.
Fraud detection decision code indicating a transaction was flagged for manual or further review before a final action is taken.
Fraud detection decision code indicating a transaction was declined or stopped due to suspected fraud.
The outcome or verdict assigned to a transaction by the fraud detection engine, mapped to database column fraud_detection_event.decision.
Authentication method code indicating no authentication was applied to the transaction.
Authentication method code indicating the transaction went through a 3D Secure challenged flow, requiring the cardholder to actively verify their identity.
Authentication method code indicating the transaction was processed without any 3D Secure authentication.
Authentication method code indicating the transaction was authenticated via 3D Secure frictionless flow, where the cardholder was not prompted to interact.
Channel code representing transactions made in-person at a physical warehouse or retail location.
Channel code representing transactions originating from a membership subscription renewal process.
Channel code representing transactions made through an online or digital commerce platform.
Fraud vector code representing fraud where a victim was psychologically manipulated into authorising a transaction or revealing sensitive information.
Fraud vector code representing fraud on transactions where the physical card was not presented, typically online or phone-based purchases.
Loss category code representing cases where a legitimate cardholder disputes a transaction they actually authorised, often to obtain a chargeback.
Loss category code representing genuine third-party fraud where an unauthorised actor used stolen credentials or card data to make a transaction.
The monetary value of losses attributed to fraudulent transactions, mapped to database column fraud_loss.loss_amount.
A reversal of a payment transaction initiated by the card issuer on behalf of the cardholder, often resulting in a fraud loss recorded in fraud_loss.loss_amount.
FX exposure direction code indicating a short position, where the entity has sold or owes a foreign currency — exposed to losses if that currency appreciates.
FX exposure direction code indicating a long position, where the entity holds or is owed a foreign currency — exposed to losses if that currency depreciates.
The total notional value of FX positions before netting or hedging offsets, mapped to fx_exposure_forecast.gross_exposure_amount.
The future date or month for which an FX exposure is projected, mapped to fx_exposure_forecast.forecast_period.
The date on which a fraud loss event occurred or was recorded, mapped to fraud_loss.loss_date.
The method or mechanism by which fraud was perpetrated, mapped to fraud_loss.fraud_vector.
The categorical label assigned to a fraud loss indicating whether it is friendly fraud or true fraud, mapped to fraud_loss.loss_category.
The channel through which a transaction was initiated (e.g. in-warehouse, ecommerce, membership renewal), mapped to fraud_loss.channel.
The method used to verify the cardholder's identity during a transaction, mapped to fraud_loss.auth_method.

A financial contract to exchange currencies at a predetermined rate on a future settlement date. Represented in the fx_forward table. Users may refer to these as forwards, forward contracts, or FX deals.
The exchange rate between two currencies at a given point in time. Stored in the fx_rate table. Users may refer to it as the conversion rate, currency rate, or forex rate.
The current market exchange rate for immediate currency delivery. Stored as the code SPOT in fx_rate.rate_type. Users may say 'spot' or 'spot price' when referring to this rate type.
The exchange rate recorded at the close of a trading day. Stored as the code CLOSING in fx_rate.rate_type. Users may refer to it as the end-of-day rate or EOD rate.
The average exchange rate over a defined period, stored as the code AVG in fx_rate.rate_type. Commonly used for period-based reporting such as MTD or YTD blended rates.

A time-based grouping used to categorise FX exposures or forwards by their remaining maturity or settlement horizon (e.g. 0-1M, 1-3M, 3-6M). Users may call these maturity buckets, time buckets, or duration bands.
Tenor bucket representing exposures or deals with a maturity or settlement date within 0 to 1 month. Full label is '0 to 1 Month'. Used in fx_exposure_forecast.tenor_bucket.
Tenor bucket representing exposures or deals with a maturity or settlement date between 1 and 3 months. Full label is '1 to 3 Months'. Used in fx_exposure_forecast.tenor_bucket.
Tenor bucket representing exposures or deals with a maturity or settlement date between 3 and 6 months. Full label is '3 to 6 Months'. Used in fx_exposure_forecast.tenor_bucket.
A deal/trade status indicating the FX forward contract has been completed and funds have been exchanged. Stored as the code SETTLED in fx_forward.status.
A deal/trade status indicating the FX forward contract has been voided and will not be executed. Stored as the code CANCELLED in fx_forward.status.
The date on which an FX forward deal is executed or booked. Stored in fx_forward.trade_date. Users may refer to it as the execution date, booking date, deal date, or entry date.

The future date on which an FX forward contract is due for settlement or delivery of funds. Stored in fx_forward.value_date. Users commonly call this the settlement date, maturity date, or delivery date.
The date on which a specific FX rate is effective or was observed. Stored in fx_rate.rate_date. Users may refer to it as the effective date, valuation date, pricing date, or as-of date.
A unique identifier for an FX forward contract. Stored in fx_forward.deal_id. Users may refer to it as trade ID, deal reference, contract ID, transaction ID, or forward ID.

General Ledger account used to record financial transactions. Referenced in the gl_account table. Users may refer to it by its code (GL code, chart of accounts code) or description (account name, ledger description).
Abbreviation for General Ledger account code. Stored in gl_account.code. Users may call it account code, account number, chart of accounts code, or ledger code.
General Ledger. The central accounting record of a company. Maps to gl_balance and gl_reconciliation tables; gl_account_ref identifies individual ledger accounts.
The monetary value held in a GL account at a point in time. Users may say 'balance', 'ledger balance', 'book value', etc.; all map to gl_balance.amount.
The current state of a GL reconciliation record. Users may say 'match status', 'recon state', etc.; maps to gl_reconciliation.status with values MATCHED or INVESTIGATING.
The unique identifier for a hedge relationship. Users may call it a 'hedge reference' or 'relationship code'; maps to hedge_relationship.code.
A reconciliation status indicating the GL balance agrees with the external or sub-ledger source with no outstanding difference. Maps to gl_reconciliation.status = 'MATCHED'.
A reconciliation status indicating an open break or discrepancy under review. Maps to gl_reconciliation.status = 'INVESTIGATING'.
The official currency of the Eurozone. Users saying 'Euro' or 'EUR' map to currency_code = 'EUR' in gl_balance and variance_currency = 'EUR' in gl_reconciliation.
The official currency of the United States. Users saying 'US Dollar', 'dollar', or 'USD' map to currency_code = 'USD' in gl_balance and variance_currency = 'USD' in gl_reconciliation.
The official currency of the United Kingdom. Users saying 'British Pound', 'pound sterling', or 'GBP' map to currency_code = 'GBP' in gl_balance and variance_currency = 'GBP' in gl_reconciliation.
The official currency of Mexico. Users saying 'Mexican Peso' or 'MXN' map to currency_code = 'MXN' in gl_balance and variance_currency = 'MXN' in gl_reconciliation.
The official currency of Japan. Users saying 'Japanese Yen' or 'JPY' map to currency_code = 'JPY' in gl_balance and variance_currency = 'JPY' in gl_reconciliation.
The official currency of Brazil. Users saying 'Brazilian Real' or 'BRL' map to currency_code = 'BRL' in gl_balance and variance_currency = 'BRL' in gl_reconciliation.
A reconciliation item where the variance_amount is non-zero and the status is INVESTIGATING in gl_reconciliation. Measures the number or total value of unresolved differences.
The last calendar day of a given month, typically used as the balance_date in gl_balance or as_of_date in gl_reconciliation for period-close reporting.
Highest credit quality rating assigned to investment instruments, indicating minimal credit risk. Maps to the 'AAA' value in investment_instrument.rating.
AAA rating specifically designated for money market funds, a distinct rating code in investment_instrument.rating.
High credit quality rating, one notch below AAA, applied to investment instruments in the investment_instrument.rating field.
High credit quality rating assigned to investment instruments, indicating very low credit risk. Maps to the 'AA' value in investment_instrument.rating.
Highest short-term credit rating for investment instruments, indicating the strongest capacity to meet financial commitments. Maps to 'A-1+' in investment_instrument.rating.
Strong short-term credit rating for investment instruments, indicating a strong capacity to meet financial commitments. Maps to 'A-1' in investment_instrument.rating.
Interest that has been earned or incurred but not yet paid or received. Maps to the interest_accrual.amount field.
The date on which interest is accrued or posted to the ledger. Maps to interest_accrual.accrual_date.
The accounting value of an investment position, typically recorded at amortized cost. Maps to investment_position.book_value.
The reference date for which an investment position snapshot is recorded. Maps to investment_position.as_of_date.
A measure of an investment position's sensitivity to interest rate changes, expressed in days. Maps to investment_position.duration_days.
A unique identifier for an investment instrument within the system. Maps to investment_instrument.code.
Money Market Fund — a type of investment instrument typically rated AAA-mf, referencing the AAA money market fund rating in investment_instrument.rating.
Yield to Maturity: the total annualised return expected on a bond if held until maturity, stored as investment_position.yield_to_maturity.
Letter of Credit: a bank-issued financial instrument guaranteeing payment, represented by the letter_of_credit table.
The stated principal or nominal value of a financial instrument (investment or letter of credit) at issuance, before any draws or market fluctuations.
The current market price of an investment position, reflecting real-time or period-end valuation, stored as investment_position.market_value.
The portion of a letter of credit that has been drawn (utilised) by the beneficiary, stored as letter_of_credit.drawn_amount.
A reference principal value used for financial instruments (both investment positions and letters of credit); maps to face_amount in both investment_position and letter_of_credit tables.
The date on which a letter of credit expires and is no longer valid, stored as letter_of_credit.expiration_date.
The current lifecycle state of a letter of credit. User-facing terms map to DB codes: Open → OPEN, Drawn → DRAWN, Expired → EXPIRED; stored as letter_of_credit.status.
LC status alias: a letter of credit against which funds have been drawn by the beneficiary. Stored as 'DRAWN' in letter_of_credit.status.
LC status alias: a letter of credit that has passed its expiration date and is no longer valid. Stored as 'EXPIRED' in letter_of_credit.status.
The classification or category of a letter of credit (e.g. standby, commercial, revolving), stored as letter_of_credit.lc_type.
The unique identifier for a letter of credit record, stored as letter_of_credit.lc_number.
The face/nominal value of an investment instrument at issuance, synonymous with face_amount in investment_position.
The aggregate market value of investment holdings; maps to investment_position.market_value, potentially summed across positions.
The proportion or absolute amount of a letter of credit that has been drawn relative to its face amount; derived from letter_of_credit.drawn_amount and letter_of_credit.face_amount.
Federal Funds Rate — the overnight interbank lending rate set by the US Federal Reserve, used as a benchmark rate in treasury and liquidity management contexts.
3-Month Secured Overnight Financing Rate — a benchmark interest rate for dollar-denominated derivatives and loans, replacing LIBOR. The 3-month tenor is widely used for floating-rate instruments.
Geopolitical Risk Index — a macro indicator measuring the level of geopolitical uncertainty globally, used in treasury for risk assessment and scenario planning.
US Consumer Price Index — a macro indicator tracking the average change in prices paid by US consumers for goods and services, used as a measure of inflation in treasury forecasting.
EUR/USD Volatility — a macro indicator capturing implied or realized volatility of the Euro-to-US Dollar exchange rate, relevant for FX risk management and hedging decisions.
Brent Crude Oil Price — the international benchmark price for crude oil, used as a macro indicator to assess commodity exposure and inflation risk in treasury.
United States — the database code representing the US geographic region in macro indicator data. Users may refer to this as 'United States', 'America', or 'domestic'.
Global / Worldwide — the database code representing worldwide geographic coverage in macro indicator data. Users may refer to this as 'worldwide', 'all regions', or 'global'.
Auto Renewal — the database code for membership fees collected via automatic renewal billing, typically a recurring charge against a stored payment method.
Mail Renewal — the database code for membership fees collected via mailed renewal notices or paper-based billing.
New Signup — the database code for fees associated with brand-new membership enrollments, as opposed to renewals.
Gold membership tier — the database code representing the Gold-level membership plan.
Executive membership tier — the database code representing the Executive-level membership plan, typically a premium or higher-cost tier.
Business membership tier — the database code representing the Business-level membership plan, designed for commercial or business members.
Collected payment status — the database code indicating a membership fee was successfully collected/paid. Users may say 'paid', 'successful', or 'cleared'.
Failed payment status — the database code indicating a membership fee payment attempt was unsuccessful. Users may say 'declined', 'rejected', or 'bounced'.
Chargeback payment status — the database code indicating a membership fee was reversed by the card issuer or bank following a dispute.
Refunded payment status — the database code indicating a membership fee was returned to the member after initial collection.

Blended Rate — a weighted average interest rate or fee rate across multiple tiers, channels, or instruments. For example, the average membership fee rate blended across GOLD, EXECUTIVE, and BUSINESS tiers.
As-of Date — the reference date for which a macro indicator value or snapshot is recorded. Users may refer to this as 'report date', 'observation date', 'snapshot date', or 'effective date'.
Issued Date — the date on which a membership fee was billed or invoiced. Users may refer to this as 'billing date', 'charge date', 'invoice date', or 'transaction date'.
Detected At — the timestamp at which a payment exception was identified or flagged in the system. Users may refer to this as 'exception raised at', 'flagged at', 'identified at', or 'detection time'.
Single Euro Payments Area Credit Transfer — a European payment rail for euro-denominated credit transfers. Maps to the value SEPA_CT in payment_hub_throughput.payment_rail.
A high-value electronic funds transfer sent over interbank networks such as SWIFT or Fedwire. Maps to the value WIRE in payment_hub_throughput.payment_rail.
Payment file status indicating the file has been transmitted/sent. Maps to the code SENT in payment_file.status.
Payment file status indicating the file has been received and acknowledged. Maps to the code RECEIVED in payment_file.status.
